nodes.name: Call LLM Gateway
nodes.notes: References the 'LLM Gateway' sub-workflow BY NAME (cachedResultName), same placeholder pattern Action Extraction's and Triage Pipeline's 'Call LLM Gateway' nodes use -- workflowId.value is left blank since no live n8n instance/workflow ID exists yet. Once llm-gateway.json is imported, re-point this node at the real workflow via the resource picker. Passes { system_prompt, user_content, response_schema } per LLM Gateway's generic contract -- this node's own JSON shape is otherwise unmodified from llm-gateway.json's contract.

nodes.name: Write commitment
nodes.notes: The scalar subquery resolves counterparty_id to NULL when no matching contacts row exists (account_id + email match fails) rather than failing the INSERT -- matches this repo's 'fall back rather than throw' convention (see Resolve counterparty email's and Validate extraction result's notes). Commitments are always written even when the counterparty can't be resolved yet (counterparty_email null, or no matching contacts row): the subquery degrades to NULL, it never raises. Reuses the same 'Supabase Postgres' credential (same name + placeholder id) Action Extraction's 'Write task' and Email Normaliser's 'Upsert email' node use, per this repo's shared-credential convention.

parameters.content:
### Placeholders to fill in on import

- **Supabase Postgres** credential (name 'Supabase Postgres', placeholder id REPLACE_WITH_SUPABASE_POSTGRES_CREDENTIAL_ID) -- reuse the same credential Action Extraction's 'Write task', Triage Pipeline's write nodes, and Email Normaliser's 'Upsert email' node already hold, do not create a new one.
- 'Call LLM Gateway' targets the 'LLM Gateway' sub-workflow by name only (workflowId.value is blank) -- re-point it at the real workflow via the resource picker once llm-gateway.json is imported.
- This workflow is called NON-BLOCKING (waitForSubWorkflow: false) by Email Normaliser's (future) 'Call Commitment Extraction' branch with { email_id, subject, body, received_at, is_from_user, account_id, participants } -- received_at must match the ISO timestamp shape Email Normaliser's 'Normalize' node produces, and participants must match the { role, name, address }[] shape that same node produces (this workflow accepts it either as a native array/object or, defensively, as a JSON string).
- Deliberately NO error-logging database write this phase: there is no 'commitment_extraction_error' column on emails (action_extraction_error/triage_error are extraction-specific to other workflows), and adding one is a schema change out of scope for this task -- 'Format error output' just formats { email_id, extracted: false } for the caller instead of writing anywhere.
- No pinData is included here by design -- pin mock data directly on nodes in the n8n editor when testing.
